new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is penultimate unless that syllable peak is /ɨ/, in which case stress moves leftward until it reaches a vowel other than /ɨ/.
new_statements.citation: Carlson, Terry. 1993. Tainae (Ivori) Organised Phonology Data. Ukarumpa: SIL Papua New Guinea. 4 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 42358.)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE:, p.3, heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)': 'Stress is penultimate unless that syllable peak is /ɨ/, in which case stress moves leftward until it reaches a vowel other than /ɨ/.' Confirmed verbatim from my own 150-dpi render of p.3 (the PDF text layer drops the barred-i glyph, printing '/ /'; the render shows /ɨ/ both times). Nothing else on tone or length; the bolded syllables in the following 'Syllable Patterns' table mark the exemplified syllable type in initial/medial/final position (OPD template), not stress, so they are not stress data. IDENTITY: OPD header 'Tainae (Ivori) Language [AGO], Kotidanga - Gulf Province, Trans New Guinea Phylum; Angan Stock-level Family,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress on the penultimate syllable; if the penult's nucleus is the high central vowel /ɨ/, stress retracts leftward to the nearest syllable whose vowel is not /ɨ/ (i.e. penultimate with /ɨ/-avoidance, a quality-sensitive retraction).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the /ɨ/-avoidance clause. The OPD gives no exceptions list. Note: the stress-marked phonetic forms in Carlson 1991 Grammar Essentials sec. 1.4 mostly show penultimate stress ([fand'ewo], [afij'awo], [pufw'æri], [iwam'eri]) but a few trisyllables are marked with initial stress where the penult is not /ɨ/ (['animo] 'mosquito', [h'amdiro] 'snake', [n'agubwɪ] 'river (goal)'), so the OPD rule is a generalisation that the 1991 transcriptions do not follow without residue.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word (OPD suprasegmentals section; examples are citation forms). No tone or contrastive length reported; the section heading 'tone, stress, length' is the OPD template and only stress is filled in.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Carlson sources describe Tainae (also called Ivori), Kotidanga, Gulf Province, villages Piu, Kamanakwawa, Paingoni = Glottolog tain1253 / ISO ago; Grammar Essentials says data come from speakers 'representative of the various dialects within the language', no single dialect singled out.
